common_name: Earth Song Rose (Fragrant Deep Pink Cold-Hardy Own-Root Shrub Rose)

planting.note: Plant bare-root or container roses in late winter or early spring in slightly acidic, well-amended, well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Earth Song is a Griffith Buck-bred rose from Iowa State University, prized for large fragrant blooms on a cold-hardy own-root shrub.

directions: Plant in slightly acidic, well-amended, well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Earth Song bears large, double, deep rose-pink blooms with a strong, sweet fragrance on a compact, bushy, own-root shrub bred at Iowa State University by Griffith Buck for reliable performance through harsh Midwestern winters without winter protection. It reblooms through the growing season with only moderate care, tolerating black spot and other common rose diseases far better than older hybrid teas. Because it grows on its own roots, any winter dieback simply regrows true to type rather than reverting to rootstock. Deadhead spent blooms to encourage continued flowering, and prune moderately in late winter to shape the plant.
sources: Iowa State University — Griffith Buck Rose Introductions
